items.title: John Altman interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 14, 2023
items.q: which starred the totally unlikely combination of David Bowie and Marlene Dietrich.

ctx.x: Really early on actually, because I became the sort of arranger-in-chief for a band called the Pasadena Roof Orchestra, who were a 1920s revival band. And they did a lot of either original songs of the ‘20s, or takedowns of McKinney’s Cotton Pickers or early Ellington. And I’d do both. I’d do original arrangements from scratch, but I’d also take down classic big band charts. When I say big band I mean pre-Swing Era charts. And

their tuba player did all the copying. And he became my copyist basically through forty- odd years. So I was never writing music just for the sake of writing music. I was always employed to do stuff. And in fact the Pasadena Roof Orchestra were hired to do the music for a film called “Just a Gigolo” which starred the totally unlikely combination of David Bowie and Marlene Dietrich. So if you can get your head round that, you can get your head round — it was a terrible film. But basically I was arranging 1920s…
Ah, you’re anticipating a question I’m going to ask later about music and emotions and all that, but I wanted to talk briefly about — do you call them jingles?
